items.title: CONTRAMEM: Learning Self-Evolving Procedural Memory from Contrasting Multi-Model Trajectories
items.title_zh: CONTRAMEM：从对比式多模型轨迹中学习自演化程序性记忆
items.summary: CONTRAMEM is a training-free framework that treats same-task outcome variation across heterogeneous model trajectories as supervision, distilling differences in correctness, efficiency, recovery and failure modes into a compact bank of app-level Function Cards and task-level Skill Cards that evolves through localized curation. On held-out GAIA2/ARE computer-use tasks it more than doubles success across three source models (26.2% to 55.3%) and transfers unchanged to the unseen Qwen3.7 Plus (18.5% to 35.5%).

items.title: Clinical Graph-JEPA: Predictive Patient-State Knowledge Graphs for Cognitive Decision Support
items.title_zh: Clinical Graph-JEPA：面向认知决策支持的预测性患者状态知识图谱
items.summary: The framework builds an evidence-scored patient-state knowledge graph per admission from structured MIMIC-IV records and inferred clinical cross-links, combining multi-agent relation proposal, ontology-aware normalization, deterministic evidence scoring and JEPA-based latent refinement. Under a leakage-free leave-one-out protocol, injecting real discharge-note representations only into note-grounded entities improves overall MRR by 31% relative.

items.title: Coalition-Aware Skill Reliability for Self-Evolving Agents
items.title_zh: 面向自演化智能体的联盟感知技能可靠性
items.summary: The authors audit agent skill banks across alternative compositions and deployment domains and identify two reliability failures: coalition pollution, where bank-level gains hide negative coalition-level skill contributions, and cross-domain utility reversal after transfer. They propose Coalition-Aware Skill Selection using sampled Shapley marginals and an unsupervised skill-masking optimizer, which improve task performance and cross-domain generalization on LoCoMo, LongMemEval, HotpotQA and ALFWorld.

items.title: Claim-Level Confidence Calibration for Reliable Decision Making with Large Language Models
items.title_zh: 面向 LLM 可靠决策的断言级置信度校准
items.summary: The paper decomposes each LLM response into atomic, verifiable claims and assigns each claim a calibrated confidence from inference-time consistency and self-verification signals, operating in closed-box settings without logits or fine-tuning. Across TriviaQA and TruthfulQA with six recent models, claim-level decomposition with post-hoc calibration reduces expected calibration error on factual questions but exposes failure modes on adversarial false-premise questions.

items.title: GeoRisk-RAG: A Hierarchy-Aware Risk Framework for Improving RAG Reliability through Selective Answering
items.title_zh: GeoRisk-RAG：通过选择性回答提升 RAG 可靠性的层次感知风险框架
items.summary: GeoRisk-RAG estimates geographic applicability before generating a response, using a DAG-based distance over geographic hierarchies to decide when to answer selectively in natural-hazard domains. On a held-out wildfire QA dataset it cuts false-confidence rates to 0.009 versus about 0.090 for semantic-similarity and reranking baselines, while achieving higher human preference alignment.

items.title: Small Reasoning Models are Instruction Followers in Function Calling
items.title_zh: 小型推理模型在函数调用中是指令遵循者
items.summary: The paper shows that LLMs achieve higher function-calling accuracy in instruction-following contexts than in tool-calling contexts, and proposes Instruction-Followed Function Calling (IFFC), which decouples function-calling logic from the primary model and delegates it to a smaller dedicated model. IFFC outperforms native and prompt-based function calling, with particularly strong gains on reasoning-oriented LLMs, and remains robust under aggressive quantization for on-device deployment.

items.title: From Diagnosis to Redesign: Using Quantitative Ethnography to Improve Multi-Agent LLM Reasoning
items.title_zh: 从诊断到重设计：用定量民族志改进多智能体 LLM 推理
items.summary: The authors apply Epistemic Network Analysis to the discourse of a five-agent debate system used for automated essay scoring, finding that correct decisions featured rubric-grounded justification, agreement and elaboration while incorrect ones featured extended proposition-challenge-response exchanges less tied to rubric criteria. Prompt revisions based on these findings raised exact scoring accuracy from 27.78% to 40.28% and shifted the discourse of incorrect debates toward the pattern of correct ones.

items.title: Learning Generalizable Behaviors for Terminal Agents
items.title_zh: 为终端智能体学习可泛化行为
items.summary: The paper proposes the Agentic Compositional Generalization hypothesis, that RL mainly shapes high-level decision-making which composes and routes skills acquired during pretraining and SFT, and introduces River, a recipe that filters low-quality environments and augments outcome rewards with process-level behavior regularization. River reaches the best performance among evaluated open-source RL-trained 8B models on four terminal-agent benchmarks and improves RL gains by 106% and 30% using fewer than 30% of the TMax training environments.

items.title: My agent.md to improve LLM-assisted code quality
items.title_zh: 我的 agent.md：提升 LLM 辅助编码质量的实践
items.summary: A developer recounts trying LLM-assisted coding in mid-2025 on a Rust mDNS project, where the generated code would not compile, then revisiting LLMs in January 2026, when a model wrote a complex indexed-binary heap class and traced an obscure bug in the polling crate linked to Windows IOCP.
